title: Credit Administration Schedule: Limit Increase Seasoning and Step Size, Personal Credit Cards
content:
A credit limit increase on Personal Credit Cards is governed by three tier figures: the whole months the account must have been open before an increase may be requested, the whole months that must pass between one increase and the next, and the largest single increase expressed as a percentage of the current limit.

| Tier | Whole months open before an increase may be requested | Whole months between increases | Largest single increase |
|---|---|---|---|
| Secured Visa | not offered | 6 | not offered |
| College Rewards Visa | 6 | 6 | 25 percent |
| Platinum Low Rate Visa | 6 | 6 | 50 percent |
| Cash Rewards Visa | 6 | 6 | 50 percent |
| Travel Rewards Visa Signature | 6 | 6 | 50 percent |
| Visa Infinite Private Client | 6 | 6 | 100 percent |

Secured Visa is the one tier for which the seasoning figure and the step size read "not offered". On the five tiers that carry them, the seasoning is 6 whole months since opening and the interval between increases is 6 whole months without exception; what separates the tiers is the step size, 25 percent on College Rewards Visa, 50 percent on the three middle tiers, and 100 percent on Visa Infinite Private Client.
